label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

report.summary: Outbox deliveries stalled because the consumer rejected many attempts with HTTP 401, so notifications were delayed. The cause of the 401s and their timing against the stall are not directly shown.

findings.claim: Outbox publication stalled (0 per 10 s for ~13 buckets) then caught up at 81 per bucket while arrivals stayed steady; pending peaked at 278.
findings.reason: Per-bucket arrivals vs publications and the pending samples show a backlog building and then draining.

findings.claim: 1007 of 1508 delivery attempts got auth errors (HTTP 401) from the consumer; only 501 succeeded. Failures were fast (~71 ms), not timeouts.
findings.reason: Outcome counts and timings show 401s answered quickly by the consumer's auth step, so the delay is retries and not a slow consumer.

findings.claim: The transfer API, DB pool and DB locks look healthy, so the delay is in outbox-to-consumer delivery and not in transfer processing.
findings.reason: Transfers returned 201 at p95 0.24 s with no 5xx, no pool timeouts or pending borrowers, and no blocking sessions.

findings.claim: A pre-existing backlog of 296 FAILED events (oldest undelivered ~6000 s) was not retried in the window, so those customers' notifications stay very late.
findings.reason: The failed count is flat at 296 and the oldest age keeps growing. Max attempts is 8, so FAILED rows are likely not retried.

limitations: Only the earliest 100 of 1508 attempt records are listed, so 401 timing against the publication gap is not shown directly.
No evidence on why the consumer rejects credentials (token or config change); the config shows no consumer auth settings.
next_checks: Query delivery logs by time for 19:20:30-19:23:00 to confirm that 401s coincide with the zero-publication buckets.
Check the consumer's auth configuration or token rotation, and whether the 296 FAILED rows need a manual requeue.

alternatives.reason: Only the earliest 100 attempt records were listed, so attempts during the zero-publication gap are not visible.
alternatives.hypothesis: Poller or scheduler stall in LedgerCore (not consumer auth) caused the zero-publication gap.

alternatives.reason: No acquisition timeouts, no pending borrowers and no blocking were observed.
alternatives.hypothesis: Database or connection pool contention delayed publishing.
